repo.description:
## Impact

The MCP workflow-validation tool evaluates caller-supplied code in the main process through an interpreter that reads inherited properties and allows assignment onto shared prototypes. A member holding only a read grant can replace a built-in method with one that returns a truthy value, which makes a server-side permission check accept a scope they do not hold. The reporter drove this to a full takeover of the instance owner's account. Accounts protected by MFA are not affected.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 2.41.4 and 2.42.1. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Disable the instance-level MCP server if it is not required.
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Enable MFA on all owner and admin accounts to prevent password-reset links from being usable even if obtained.
- Audit and revoke `workflow:read` MCP OAuth grants from any users who do not require them.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.
repo.summary: Shared Prototype Mutation Through the MCP Workflow-Validation Interpreter Allows Owner Account Takeover
